headline: High data-leakage and compliance risk: Dexter’s broad egress can expose financial data into Khoj’s indexed notes/search workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files, so content can cross from A to B through a shared file-like workflow. Khoj’s retrieval/chat can treat stored text as context, making prompt injection plausible even without MCP or clipboard. No direct evidence of a shared channel beyond files, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Dexter writes attacker-controlled instructions into files that Khoj indexes or reads
IF Khoj treats retrieved note content as authoritative chat context
mitigations: Keep Dexter and Khoj on separate directories
Disable indexing of Dexter scratchpad paths
Add a manual review step before Khoj ingests new files
Use read-only exports from Dexter into a quarantined folder
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to retrieved chunks

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter has broad network egress and calls multiple external APIs while touching financial and market data. Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files and also uses cloud or configured search providers. If Dexter outputs sensitive financial data into files or prompts that Khoj indexes, that data can flow into third-party services through B’s retrieval/search path. The pairwise leakage pathway is credible in default use.
conditions: IF Dexter stores financial data in .dexter/scratchpad/ or sends it to external APIs
IF Khoj indexes those files and then queries cloud or configured search providers
mitigations: Exclude financial-data folders from Khoj indexing
Rotate or scope Dexter API keys to non-sensitive test data
Use a separate self-hosted Khoj instance with external search disabled
Review indexed documents for sensitive fields before sync
requires-engineering: enforce data-class-based routing between the agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and autonomous execution, while Khoj supports multiple instances with shared index across the user’s clients. That creates overlapping writes to a shared mutable retrieval corpus even though Khoj cannot write files directly. The conflict is less severe than same-dir filesystem writes, but concurrent updates can still race and corrupt or stale-index shared state.
conditions: IF multiple Dexter instances write outputs that Khoj indexes concurrently
IF Khoj clients share the same index while Dexter updates source files
mitigations: Serialize Dexter runs that feed the same index
Pause Khoj reindexing during Dexter writes
Use per-run output directories for Dexter
Snapshot the index before bulk ingestion
requires-engineering: add locking around shared index updates

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter’s autonomous execution can generate outputs that Khoj later retrieves and presents in chat. Khoj’s RAG workflow can surface those outputs without a built-in verification step, so errors or hallucinations from A can cascade into B’s answers. There is no evidence Khoj automatically acts on them, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Dexter-generated text is indexed by Khoj
IF Khoj answers users from retrieved Dexter output without manual verification
mitigations: Mark Dexter outputs as untrusted in the index
Require source links in Khoj responses
Add a human review step for high-stakes answers
Limit Dexter outputs to summaries, not assertions
requires-engineering: implement retrieval-time confidence filtering

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter touches financial data and market data, while Khoj indexes personal notes/files. If financial records or regulated personal data are placed into Khoj’s shared index, retention and residency obligations can diverge from Dexter’s external API usage and Khoj’s cloud or configured search providers. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated financial records are indexed into Khoj
IF Khoj uses cloud search providers or external APIs for those records
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Khoj indexes
Use self-hosted providers only for sensitive corpora
Set short retention on indexed notes
Document a data-handling policy for both tools
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls per corpus
